svg.aria-label: How to write ં: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ં
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ં (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/10_kam.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the anusvara drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source note on variation: In the template for કં, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ં is one pen-down run: a small closed loop that starts at its top and turns anticlockwise. The printed dot is solid, so the pen path circles inside it. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 156 of its 157 stored prototypes of the anusvara are one stroke, 72% of them anticlockwise. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
